'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Gunmen ambush a column of a civilian militia in [[Loroum Province|Loroum]], [[Burkina Faso]], killing 41 people. It is one of the deadliest single-day attack against the militia. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/two-day-mourning-period-declared-after-41-killed-burkina-faso-ambush-2021-12-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Madagascar shipwreck]]
**Twenty-four more people are found dead after the boat accident off the coast of [[Analanjirofo]], [[Madagascar]], three days ago, bringing the total death toll to 85. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20211223-death-toll-from-madagascar-shipwreck-rises-to-85 (France 24)]
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**Eleven people are dead as a boat carrying migrants sinks in the [[Aegean Sea]]. Around 90 other people are rescued. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/12/24/seven-people-killed-in-shipwreck-off-greek-islet (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] in a person who travelled from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://thescoop.co/2021/12/23/brunei-reports-first-omicron-case/ (''The Scoop'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****The [[Kuwait]]i Directorate General of Civil Aviation announces that all citizens who wish to travel, but who were fully vaccinated more than nine months ago, must receive a [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] beginning on January 2. [https://timesofoman.com/article/110939-booster-shot-mandatory-for-travel-for-kuwaiti-citizens-vaccinated-9-months-ago (''Times of Oman'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 drug development]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] approves the emergency use of the [[Molnupiravir]] drug made by [[Merck & Co.]] for high-risk adult patients and also approves the use of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/philippines-approves-mercks-covid-19-pill-for-at-risk-patients (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Singapore]] suspends new ticket sales for the quarantine-free Vaccinated Travel Lane until January 20 in an attempt to reduce the number of imported cases of the Omicron variant. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/12/22/singapore-to-suspend-new-ticket-sales-for-quarantine-free-travel.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 109 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 5,015. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Health/wireStory/korea-marks-deadliest-day-pandemic-omicron-looms-81909733 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****[[Prime Minister of Andorra|Prime Minister]] [[Xavier Espot]] tests positive for COVID-19 with mild symptoms. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2021/12/23/xavier_espot_positiu_per_covid_192572_1125.html (''Diari d’Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports a record 91,608 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set in November 2020. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-23/france-has-record-new-covid-19-cases-as-omicron-spreads (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports its first confirmed death related to the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-germany-records-first-death-from-omicron-variant/a-60241594 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The [[Italy|Italian]] [[Government of Italy|government]] announces a ban of [[New Year's Eve]] celebrations as well as all mass gatherings and closes nightclubs and bars until the end of January. The government also agree to reintroduce [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mandatory mask wearing]] outdoors and will reduce the validity of vaccine certificate to six months beginning from February 1. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-12-italy-outdoor-mask-compulsory.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports its first two cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant, prompting the health ministry to ban all standing events except for weddings and funerals beginning on December 17 and restrict entry to the hospitality sector and sporting events to only those with a valid [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic|vaccine certificate]]. A 1 a.m. curfew will also be imposed for all businesses beginning on January 17. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/omicron-cases-found-in-malta-stand-up-events-banned-from-monday.923398 (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] surpasses 600,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russias-coronavirus-death-toll-tops-600000-2021-12-23/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 119,789 new cases of COVID-19. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-records-119-789-new-coronavirus-cases-highest-daily-figure-since-start-of-pandemic-12502939 (Sky News)]
****Preliminary data from the United Kingdom suggests the [[hospitalization]] rate of the COVID-19 Omicron variant is between 50% to 70% lower than the [[Delta variant]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-omicron-variant-has-50-70-less-hospitalization-rate/a-60245366 (Deutsche Welle)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras]]
****[[Honduras]] begins administering a booster dose of the COVID-19 vaccine for all adults aged above 18 years using the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/honduras-begins-giving-covid-19-booster-shots-all-adults-2021-12-23/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration]] grants [[emergency use authorization]] for [[Merck & Co.]]'s antiviral COVID-19 oral pill named [[Molnupiravir]] for at-risk individuuals. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8470537/mercks-covid-19-pill-approved-u-s-fda/ (Global News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
****[[Argentina]] receives more than 2.6 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for use as [[booster dose]]s. [https://www.lavoz.com.ar/ciudadanos/llegaron-al-pais-mas-de-dos-millones-de-dosis-de-vacuna-moderna-para-completar-esquemas/ (''La Vos'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Ecuador]]
****[[Ecuador]]'s Minister of Public Health announces that the COVID-19 vaccination will be mandatory for all citizens over the age of 5 years unless they have a medical exemption due to the spread of [[SARS-CoV-2 variants]] and an increase in the number of new cases. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-59772299 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****[[New South Wales]] reports a record 5,715 cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant becoming the dominant strain in the state. The [[NSW Government]] reintroduces mask-wearing in indoor settings, despite the state having a 93.5% vaccination rate. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-12-23/nsw-records-5715-cases-and-1-death-covid-19/100721460/ (ABC News Australia)]
****[[Australia]] reports a record 8,697 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set on December 22. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-03-17/coronavirus-cases-data-reveals-how-covid-19-spreads-in-australia/12060704 (ABC News Australia)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United States relations]]
**[[Uyghur genocide]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs the [[Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act]] into law banning imports from [[China]]'s [[Xinjiang]] region citing concerns about the use of [[forced labour]]. China denies [[Human rights in China|human rights]] abuses in Xinjiang. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/12/23/biden-signs-law-banning-goods-made-with-forced-labour-from-china (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Japan–United States relations]], [[Taiwan–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] and [[Japan]] approve a plan for a joint military operation in response to a possible "Taiwan emergency". The operation would consist of deploying [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marines]] on the [[Ryukyu Islands]] near [[Taiwan]], while the [[Japan Self-Defense Forces]] would provide logistical support such as ammunition and fuel supplies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/japan-us-draw-up-joint-operation-plan-any-taiwan-emergency-kyodo-2021-12-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[14-Year-Old Valentina Orellana-Peralta killed in LAPD response]]
**While responding to multiple reports of a violent assault suspect at a [[Los Angeles]] clothing store, [[LAPD]] officers fired upon one male subject. Valentina Orellana-Peralta was sheltering with her mother and other patrons and was killed by an errant shot. Valentina and the suspect both succumbed to their injuries in the store. Several patrons were injured by the suspect prior to officers' arrival. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/12/28/us/lapd-teen-killed-valentina-orellana-peralta-family/index.html]
*[[Killing of Daunte Wright]]
**Former Minneapolis police officer Kim Potter is found guilty on both counts in the [[Killing of Daunte Wright|killing of Daunte Wright]]. She is scheduled to be sentenced on February 18, 2022. [https://apnews.com/article/kim-potter-guilty-manslaughter-death-of-daunte-wright-43e70645189bf61be64fc00534adf388 (''AP'')]
*[[Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lithuania]]
***The [[Seimas]] votes 89–17 with 19 abstentions to approve a law that would require [[Member of Parliament|MP]]s to have a health pass, which shows proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination in Lithuania|vaccination]], a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test result]] from the previous 72 hours, or that a person has recovered from COVID-19, in order to attend hearings beginning in January. [https://www.barrons.com/news/lithuania-to-require-covid-health-pass-from-mps-01640284207?tesla=y (''Barron's'')]
*[[Workfare]]
**The [[Australian Government]] pays a [[Australian dollar|A$]]2,000,000 settlement to the [[Shire of Ngaanyatjarraku]] to end a [[class action]] lawsuit in the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]] over the controversial [[Work for the Dole|Community Development Program]], which saw unemployed [[Ngaanyatjarra]] and other [[Indigenous Australians|Indigenous Australian]] people in remote communities working up to 25 hours a week otherwise unpaid in order to receive the [[Social security in Australia#JobSeeker Payment|JobSeeker]] payment, which is generally considered to be less than the [[cost of living]] and which is provided to other Australians in exchange for completing a fortnightly quota of job applications. The Ngaanyatjarra accused the program of being [[Racism in Australia|racist]] and a form of [[Slavery in the 21st century|modern slavery]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/dec/23/federal-government-to-pay-out-2m-to-settle-class-action-over-racist-work-for-the-dole-program (''The Guardian'')]
